quick.html:
Try to always be in multiball. The right ramp spells Diner which lights the lock under the left ramp, but if you avoid shooting the right ramp when it's lit for Stir the Cup, Diner letters will be preserved and it will only take one shot to re-light locks after multiball instead of 5. During multiball, make Rush 1 and Rush 2 at the upper right and lower right scoops to light ramps for 500,000 for the rest of multiball. Dine-Time, this game's Jackpot, is raised by left ramp combos or lit in lanes, and is lit at the spinner or right saucer after all 5 customers have been served via the drop targets or ramps that have been lit for Food by completing the top lanes.

sections.title: Quick strategy synopsis
sections.html:
Try to always be in multiball. The right ramp spells Diner which lights the lock under the left ramp, but if you avoid shooting the right ramp when it's lit for Stir the Cup, Diner letters will be preserved and it will only take one shot to re-light locks after multiball instead of 5. During multiball, make Rush 1 and Rush 2 at the upper right and lower right scoops to light ramps for 500,000 for the rest of multiball. Dine-Time, this game's Jackpot, is raised by left ramp combos or lit in lanes, and is lit at the spinner or right saucer after all 5 customers have been served via the drop targets or ramps that have been lit for Food by completing the top lanes.

The below picture of Diner's playfield was taken from the VPX recreation by Flupper.

children.title: Skill shot
children.html: The skill shot is pure timing, and awards whatever point value is lit times the current ball number. There is no "spot customer" option at a lower value like there is for the Spinout on Taxi, so there's no reason not to go for the No. 1 option every time for 150,000 points. The plunge should end up in the top left saucer, and if it does, the skill shot value will be awarded then, but if somehow the ball misses that saucer, the skill shot will be awarded when the ball goes through a top lane. Every plunger strength can vary, but letting go of a full plunge right when the light moves from 75,000 to 50,000 has a good chance of earning the No. 1.

children.title: E-A-T top lanes
children.html:
Spelling E-A-T advances the bonus multiplier, lights one of the in lanes for Advance Dine-Time, and lights both of the ramps for Food. After the bonus multiplier reaches 5x, completing the top lanes scores an E-A-T Bonus worth 100,000, increasing by 100,000 each time up to 500,000. The first 5 E-A-T Bonuses also increase the bonus multiplier one at a time up to 10x, but the game will never display the bonus multiplier as being higher than 5x.
Both flippers can be used to move the E-A-T lights via lane change, but they both move the lights in the same direction; there is no backwards lane change.

children.title: Food and customers
children.html:
There are 5 characters across the playfield: Haji, Babs, Boris, Pepe, and Buck. Each one has a different diner order that consists of two food items; it will always be one food item corresponding to each of the two banks of drop targets, center and left. Completing one bank awards that food, and completing both banks finishes their order. (The current customer always flashes, while lit ones have been served.) Making a ramp that is lit for Food spots one food item, allowing you to skip one drop target completion.

Each customer served adds a 1% tip to the end of the ball, explained later during the Bonus and bonus multiplier section. Serving all 5 customers immediately lights Dine-Time for 15 seconds, which is this game's jackpot (explained in detail later). If Dine-Time is failed, the 5th customer will send their food back and need to be re-served. If Dine-Time is collected, all characters will unlight and can be worked through again, building up an end of ball tip of 5% or higher.

children.title: Left ramp
children.html:
Awards a cash register bonus. The cash register starts at 20,000 points, and advances by an additional 20,000 if the ramp is made again within 10 seconds. The cash register maxes out at 300,000 points. If the 100,000 level is reached, the Grill target to the left of the bumpers is lit for an extra ball (once per ball in play), and subsequent loops to the left ramp will score the value lit above the ramp as well as adding 1,000,000 points to Dine-Time per shot until the ramp times out. If multiple values are lit above the ramp, shooting the ramp scores the sum of all lit values.
This ramp is lit to spot Food by completing the E-A-T lanes.

children.title: Right ramp
children.html:
The right ramp lights Diner letters, scoring 25,000 for the D, 50,000 for I, 75,000 for N, 100,000 for E, and 250,000 for R. Completing the word Diner lights the lock under the left ramp and lights this ramp for Stir the Cup for a few seconds. During Stir the Cup, the ball will spin around the whirlpool in the back of the playfield, scoring big points based on how much the cup spins- 250,000 at base level, an additional 250,000 for every two spins, 2,500,000 for ten spins, and an additional 100,000 for every spin after that. Stirring the Cup is decent points, but it also unlights all of the Diner letters, meaning 5 more right ramp shots are required to light the lock again. However, if Diner is spelled but the cup is never stirred, it will take just 1 shot to this right ramp to relight the lock after the next multiball. In competition play, most players will elect to do this. Some will take the strategy even further, waiting for Stir the Cup to time out and not starting multiball just to take advantage of this ramp being worth 250,000 a shot when the lock is lit but Stir the Cup is not.
Like the left ramp, the right ramp is lit to spot Food after one shot after the E-A-T top lanes are completed.

children.title: Today's Special (far right saucer)
children.html: When not lit, this saucer just sends the ball up to the top of the playfield. The left in lane lights this saucer for Today's Special for a few seconds, which gives a random award: 25,000 points, 50,000, 75,000, 100,000, 250,000, serve customer, advance Dine-Time, or extra ball. If a ball is locked, though, Today's Special will almost always give Start Multiball. If a ball is locked and Today's Special gives an award other than Start Multiball, multiball will be started anyway. This saucer is also lit for Rush-2 during multiball. Today's Special is intended to eject directly to the upper saucer at the top of the table, which is also the endpoint of the Spinner lane shot, so Today's Special can also be used to collect Rush-1 during multiball, or the Dine-Time jackpot.

children.title: Multiball
children.html:
After a ball is locked under the left ramp, Multiball is eligible to begin. The standard multiball start is to shoot the spinner lane between the center drop targets and the right ramp, so that the ball lands in the top saucer. However, multiball can also be started at Today's Special saucer, since that shot sends the ball up to the top saucer as well.

During multiball, all scoring is in play, and there is no playield multiplier. Progress on Food, customers, and Dine-Time can still be made. The only multiball-specific scoring feature is Beat the Rush. comparable to the Express Lane on Taxi. Shooting Rush-1 at the spinner lane starts Beat the Rush, which lights Rush-2 for a few seconds. Making both Rush-1 and Rush-2 means you have indeed beaten the rush, and you are rewarded by both ramps having their value increased to 500,000 points for the rest of multiball. If you can start multiball, beat the rush, hold a ball on the one flipper, and use the other ball to loop a ramp all day with the right flipper, you will be on your way to a great score.

Since the Today's Special saucer is effectively tied to the top saucer at the end of the spinner lane, anything that the spinner lane would give you can be collected at the Today's Special hole, including Rush-1. If you start multiball with a shot to the lit Today's Special scoop, the kickout from Today's Special will give you Rush-1 for free, meaning all it takes to beat the rush is one more Today's Special shot. Even if Rush-1 is not given for free at the start of multiball in this way, the regular Rush-1 can be collected during multiball at Today's Special as well.

children.title: Dine-Time
children.html:
Dine-Time is this game's jackpot. The value of Dine-Time is 1,000,000 points times whatever hour the clock hand on the backglass is pointing to. Dine-Time starts each game at 1,000,000 points and is advanced by lit in lanes, the appropriate Today's Special award, or by continuing to loop the left ramp after the Cash Register has been advanced to 100,000. The maximum Dine-Time value is 12,000,000 points.

As soon as the 5th customer is served, Dine-Time is lit for 15 seconds at the spinner lane, but it can be collected with either a full shot to the spinner lane or a shot to the Today's Special hole. Once Dine-Time is collected, all 5 customers will reset, and can be served again toward a new Dine-Time (and sets of served customers are remembered, so the end of ball tip will reach or exceed 5%). If Dine-Time is failed, one of the customers will send their food back and need to be re-served for Dine-Time to light again. Completing both banks of drop targets while Dine-Time is lit scores a Drop Target Bonus worth 1,000,000 points; this is never worth going for, just shoot for the actual Dine-Time collect instead.

children.title: Grill target
children.html:
A red standup target just to the left of the bumpers, shootable between the left ramp and center drop targets. It is briefly lit immediately after completing a drop target bank to collect Food. Hitting this target when lit scores the sum of all the lit values, which totals 100,000 the first time, 250,000 the second time, 500,000 the third time, and 1,500,000 the fourth time, after which it resets to 100,000 for the fifth. There's okay points here, but the angle into the pop bumpers is incredibly dangerous.

Advancing the Cash Register value to 100,000 lights this target for an extra ball, once per ball in play.

children.title: Bonus and bonus multiplier
children.html:
The base end of ball bonus starts at 1,000 points, is increased 1,000 at a time by performing various playfield tasks (such as completing E-A-T, completing a drop target bank, locking a ball, or going down an out lane), maxes out at 99,000 points, and is multiplied by the bonus multiplier.. The bonus multiplier is advanced by the E-A-T lanes, up to a maximum of 10x; the game will not display the bonus multiplier as higher than 5 under any circumstance, but the calculation will still be correct. (Additional E-A-T lanes still light ramps for Food and such, but only directly award points.) This portion of the bonus cannot be carried ball to ball or collected mid-ball, and usually does not contribute a significant amount to scoring anyway.

More interesting than the end of ball bonus is the tip. After the bonus is added, you receive a tip of 1% for each customer served throughout the entire game. This tip is effectively a multiplier applied to your entire score up to that point, which can get pretty sizable after a Dine-Time has been collected, and is reason enough not to tilt on its own. The maximum tip is 10%. The tip ends up serving as a way to keep ball 1 important without being a simple carryover for the base bonus or the bonus multiplier, as it means customers served on a good ball 1 will continue to pay you off for the rest of the game. The tip considers your score rounded down to the nearest 10,000, so a 1% tip on a score of 1,052,100 will be 10,500, not 10,521. The score on Diner rolls over at 100,000,000 points, and there is no compensation for this; if your score is 103,000,000 and you have a 10% tip, the amount of the tip will be 300,000 instead of 10,300,000, since your score over 100,000,000 is ignored. This opens the possibility of it being preferable to intentionally drain with just under 100,000,000 points to get a large tip, instead of rolling the score, draining, and getting basically no tip.

children.title: Bottom of the table
children.html: Diner has a conventional in/out lane setup. The out lanes can be lit for extra ball, but this is purely a consolation extra ball that only lights if a player's first two balls were extremely short (and indeed if the consolation extra balls setting is on). The in lanes can be lit for Advance Dine-Time after competing the E-A-T letters. Both the consolation EB and the Dine-Time light can be moved with flipper lane change. The left in lane only also lights Today's Special on the right for a few seconds.

children.title: Settings and miscellanea
children.html:
Settings that change how the Diner near you plays include the following.

  • Whether or not Today's Special can start multiball (default is yes)
  • The time limit for Rush-2 during Beat the Rush (can be 4-25 seconds, default 20)
  • Whether or not served customers carry from ball to ball (default is yes, and only the meanest and hardest games would turn this off)
  • Whether or not lit food is carried over between balls (default is yes); regardless of this setting all drop targets reset between balls anyway
  • The difficulty of Today's Special (can be always lit, on or off at the start of each ball, and have a timer or be untimed)
  • Whether or not progress on E-A-T lanes is carried over between balls (default yes)
  • How much of Diner is needed to lock a ball (default is that all of Diner is lit at the start of the game, but the full spelling is needed for additional multiballs, unless you never stir the cup as mentioned earlier in the guide)
  • Whether or not shots to the Today's Special hole can collect awards from the spinner lane/top saucer (default is yes; again, only very hard settings or very mean operators would disable this)

Yes, the customers do always order the same things, sadly. Haji wants a hot dog and a root beer; Babs wants an iced tea and a frankfurter; Boris (who plays the same sound effect as Gorbie from Taxi) wants a burger and fries; Pepe wants the chili and a root beer; Buck wants the (Texas) chili and fries. The left drop targets always give the iced tea, root beer, or fries, while the center drop targets always give the hot dog, hamburger, or chili.
